items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: And God, we worked together for about ten years at ABC.

ctx.x: When you did an album in those days, how long did it take to do an album?

Well a session was three hours. But an album, no, that took more than three hours. It might have taken us all day. But it was “More Than You Can Stand.” It’s a long LP. That’s where I play “Saxophobia.” And then he wrote a piece called “Idyell” but it wasn’t called anything. I’ll tell you what happened. We used to do the Elgin Watch T.V. show and U.S. Steel Show. And in the studio Bernie had earphones on. And there’s a love scene going on in the movie. And a violin is playing this beautiful background music. So…
on that album “More Than You Can Stand,” called “Idyell.” Four clarinets and myself. It’s very beautiful. It only runs maybe two and a half or three minutes.

items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: And God, we worked together for about ten years at ABC.

ctx.x: Tell me about Bernie Green. Sometimes he was Bernard Greenwald?

Bernard Green yes. He was a very good conductor, very good arranger. He knew what he wanted and he got it. He was a wonderful guy. He was a little excited sometimes but nice you know. And God, we worked together for about ten years at ABC.
His son told me that he used to say, “Al is the best.”

items.title: Al Gallodoro Interview, 1966-05-10
items.q: Bernie Green, who conducted the Sid Caesar Show, he is a tremendous composer. This man has ideas.

ctx.x: And that can't be obtained at all?

Becquard? Oh, God, no. You see, sometimes we miss out on ourselves. I could buy the records at that time at distributors' price, $2.19, but who thought of buying two, three hundred albums? The same way with Columbia. You think, oh, I'll wait until next month. By that time they're gone. The company goes broke. Now this has been going on, Howard, in the record industry for years. Bernie Green, who conducted the Sid Caesar Show, he is a tremendous composer. This man has ideas. He can write anything. Spike Jonze…
